crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Drug repurposing uses AI to find new therapeutic uses for existing approved or investigational drugs. It draws on molecular simulation, electronic health records, and biomedical literature. The goal is to shorten development timelines and reduce failure risk compared with de novo drug discovery. This page covers computational screening, target matching, and clinical signal detection.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on high performance computing clusters and cloud GPU instances for molecular docking and large language model inference. Data infrastructure includes curated chemical libraries, protein structure databases, and de-identified patient record warehouses. Many groups use containerized pipelines that combine cheminformatics toolkits with graph neural network frameworks. Storage and versioning of model weights and screening results are standard.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Typical workflows start by encoding drug and target structures into numerical representations, then scoring their interaction with docking simulations or learned embeddings. Researchers also mine real world data for unexpected drug outcome associations using propensity matched cohorts or self controlled case series. Validation moves from retrospective hits to in vitro binding assays and, where warranted, existing trial data. The field relies on negative controls and calibration sets to reduce false positives.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on patient data privacy, off label promotion boundaries, and liability if a repurposed drug causes harm. Regulatory agencies expect evidence from controlled studies before new indications are approved, even when the molecule is already marketed. Provenance of training data and model predictions must be documented for audit and reproducibility. Product liability exposure can arise if a company markets an AI suggested use without adequate clinical substantiation.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward combining molecular simulation with multimodal patient data to propose repurposing candidates that are both mechanistically plausible and clinically supported. Foundation models trained on protein, chemical, and clinical text may reduce the need for bespoke feature engineering. Prospective platform trials and registry based studies are likely to test AI nominated repurposing hypotheses more quickly. The main open problem is turning computational hits into regulatory grade evidence.
